toni_devex: quick catch — customer report: Redwood SDK works in next dev but fails when deployed as Next middleware on Vercel edge. Error: "TypeError: crypto.getRandomValues is not a function".

sam_runtime: ok that's classic. are we calling crypto at module init?

toni_devex: yes, nonce generation runs during client construction at import time. also another user hit `ReferenceError: require is not defined` because their toolchain picked cjs entry.

li_ts: right now package.json uses main=cjs and module=esm but no explicit edge subpath. TS sometimes resolves to cjs d.ts. Two paths: make default import edge-safe, or add explicit subpath `redwood/edge`. Subpath seems least disruptive.

anya_prodeng: practical plan: 1) build an edge-targeted ESM bundle (no node: imports) and ship as dist/edge.mjs, 2) export subpath './edge' in package exports with types -> dist/edge.d.ts, 3) avoid top-level crypto calls (lazy-detect globalThis.crypto and fallback).

sam_runtime: add a tiny runtime helper: getRand = () => { if (globalThis.crypto?.getRandomValues) return ...; if (globalThis.crypto?.subtle) use a digest-based fallback; else throw helpful error mentioning edge import. } no sync node:crypto usage in edge bundle.

li_ts: I'll add the edge.d.ts and a CI TS resolution test `import type {Client} from 'redwood/edge'` + an esbuild bundle smoke that emulates vercel bundling.

ci-bot: CI job edge-bundle-smoke queued.

toni_devex: docs: update Next middleware quickstart to show `import {createClient} from 'redwood/edge'` and add troubleshooting blurb. Also add linter rule in templates to prefer subpath in middleware.

anya_prodeng: sounds good. timeline?

toni_devex: aiming to land as a patch this week. will post PR preview link when ready. thx everyone :thumbsup:
